status: LEGACY FORMAT — not a tessl eval scenario, and not convertible into one as written. Every assertion cites specific source facts of the fictional orchard-console app (a named tab array, a named feature flag, an exact polling contract), so a runnable scenario would require building that app as a fixture and maintaining it forever. Kept as the design record of what this skill must do. Live measurement lives in evals/ at the repo root; see CLAUDE.md > Evals.
note: The orchard-console app in these prompts is fictional — the same invented app used in references/harvest-playbook.md and references/anatomy.md. The repo path, component names, feature flags, timings and endpoints point at nothing real; they illustrate shape only.

evals.name: fr025-two-entry-paths
evals.prompt: in ~/dev/acme/orchard-console I need a clickable prototype of FR-025 to show the client. the spray-window advisory screen already exists in the app but nothing navigates to it, and we have to decide between two paths: the advisory showing up as soon as the scout opens a block, or a row inside My Account. make it a single html file that runs on the dev server and that you can actually click through
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML prototype anchored on FR-025, rebuilding My Blocks / Spray Window / Supplies / My Account from the real source (real tab list, real copy, cited tokens), with a control panel whose toggles map to CA-03/CA-07/CA-08 plus an annotation layer, real fetch through the dev-server proxy with the 202 + retryAfterSeconds contract, and a spike report at the end.

assertions.text: The block-roster tab strip reproduces the app's real static tab array from BlockRoster.tsx (All, Bearing, Dormant, Spraying, Quarantined, Retired) — no invented tab such as 'Irrigation', and no real tab silently dropped.

Every user-visible in-frame string is either findable in the app source under frontend/src/ or is marked as part of the requirement's delta (annotated). No plausible-but-absent label sits unmarked beside harvested ones.
Each app design token in :root carries a source citation of the form path:line, and any prototype-only color is separated into its own justified group.
The feature-flag control is labelled with the app's actual identifier SHOW_SPRAY_WINDOW, and its description reflects that the flag gates more than one site (entry routing AND the My Account row).

The polling implementation mirrors production useSprayWindow.ts: 3s floor, 20s default, 90-second ceiling, interval taken from the response body, chained setTimeout rather than setInterval, and no automatic retry after a failure.
The prototype does not contain an invented advisory payload presented as real. It either fetches live, inlines a genuinely captured response with its capture command, or shows a visibly-labeled stub.
Single HTML file with zero external subresources — no src to a remote host, no stylesheet, no @import, no CDN script. Inline SVG only.
An annotation toggle exists that highlights everything the requirement adds or changes relative to today's app, using a color that does not exist in the app's token set.

Control-panel toggles trace to FR-025 acceptance criteria — at minimum a failure simulation (CA-03) and the feature flag (CA-08) — and invisible criteria such as CA-05 (leaving cancels the wait) are narrated in a caption rather than silently omitted.
A spike report is produced naming what the run settled and where each answer belongs, and it does not itself write a ## Playback block, an ADR, or edits to docs/requirements/.
No file inside ~/dev/acme/orchard-console was created, modified, or deleted.

evals.name: tierC-new-screen
evals.prompt: same repo (~/dev/acme/orchard-console): I want to prototype a new 'My Loans' screen inside My Account — a list of the scout's equipment loans with status, due date, and a copy-collection-code action. the service that returns the loans DOES NOT EXIST YET, nobody has even written the contract. build me the clickable prototype anyway so I can take it to the client
evals.expected_output: A prototype that rebuilds the My Account shell at high fidelity from source, adds the new screen as an annotated delta, and uses a visibly-labeled Tier C stub for the loans data — explicitly NOT inventing a plausible payload or a fake contract, and reporting the route shape it proposes as a proposal.

assertions.text: The prototype explicitly declares that its loans data is a stub because the service does not exist — visible to the reviewer in the UI (caption or on-screen label), not merely in a code comment.
No fabricated API response shape is presented as if it were the real contract. Any proposed request/response shape is explicitly labelled a proposal awaiting confirmation.

The surrounding My Account shell (profile block, balance, tiles, section headers, existing rows, bottom nav, block bar) is rebuilt from the real source rather than approximated, with real copy strings.
The new My Loans entry point and screen are marked as the requirement's delta via the annotation layer, distinguishing them from the existing app surface.
Each app design token in :root carries a path:line citation; prototype-only colors are separated and justified.
Single HTML file with zero external subresources — inline SVG only, no CDN, no remote images or fonts.
The absence of a backend is handled as a legitimate fidelity tier rather than as a blocker — the run produces a usable clickable prototype instead of refusing or stalling.
No file inside ~/dev/acme/orchard-console was created, modified, or deleted.
